work_order.root_cause: Every safety property in this slice is enforced by a CLAIM the code and its tests each assert in isolation, and never by one mechanism both sides must call. The claim that decides the ticket is this one: a signed capability is its own authority, so the intent gate belongs at issuance and the write path only re-checks integrity. kernel.validateIntent is consequently unreachable from the only module that writes - src/executor/executor.js:201 calls kernel.validateCapability and nothing else - and the sole provenance of a delivered envelope is an HMAC over DEFAULT_SIGNING_SECRET, a literal exported from src/policy/kernel.js:22. So the gate is not on the write path, only in front of the mint, and a capability the server never issued is admitted exactly as a real one is. Four more instances of the same shape, all of which I reproduced against the branch build: the freeze KEY is derived twice (guardian.freeze's scopeId default, src/strategy/guardian.js:160, and kernel.killSwitchChecks, :365) and the two derivations agree only for the provider scope, so a freeze at global/tenant/campaign writes a row no reader ever asks for; guardian.reEnable (:206) returns a literal re_enabled:true and drops the `row` the repository handed it, and the route (:887) drops it again, so a re-enable that cleared nothing reports success; src/web/client.js:236-240 paints the receipt toast and calls window.location.reload() in the same task, so the browser navigates before the toast is ever composited; and routes.js:143 postureForClass binds an unvalidated body.action_class straight into a sqlite parameter, so an absent or object value is a 500 rather than the fail-closed 403 the kernel already answers for null.
work_order.understanding:
The previous work order was not wrong about the repository - it was greenfield and it read the code correctly - but it was wrong about the design that decides this ticket, and that premise is why four of QA's five findings are in the safety path rather than in the UI.

WHAT ATTEMPT 1 GOT WRONG, PLAINLY. The plan's alternatives_considered rejects, by name, 'Move the posture check into the executor as well as at issuance', on the grounds that 'two owners for one check, and the second is wrong: a trust row edited between issuance and execution would retroactively invalidate a correctly signed capability'. That rejection is the whole of BUG-5. The plan's own residual_risks(3) already named the exposure - 'POST /v1/actions/execute is a bearer-token surface whose only control is the signing secret, and that secret has a public dev default' - and then bounded it with 'the blast radius is bounded only by the fact that the only writable provider is an in-memory fake'. The bound was chosen backwards: the fake is what makes the money harmless, not what makes the gate unreachable. QA proved the gate itself is absent from the write path, and would have proved it against a real provider too. The premise 'a signed capability is the attestation' cannot survive a secret that is published in the repository, and the plan asserted the premise in three places at once (kernel.js:365 'a freeze is checkable by whoever holds the capability', executor.js:151 'a signed capability is the authority to write', and the rejected alternative), so the executor was built to validate integrity where it should have validated authority.

The four smaller findings are the same mistake at smaller scale: a property asserted by a test that supplied the value it was checking, so nothing compared the two sides. test/strategy/guardian.test.js:158 is titled 'THE WRITE AND READ SIDES AGREE, for all four scopes' and at :164 computes the correct scope id itself before calling freeze - so it tests the repository round trip and never freeze's own default, and the plan's residual_risks(2) claim that 'a test asserts the agreement' is false exactly where the bug is. test/api/guardian.test.js:163 asserts a wrong-scope re-enable returns 200 and, at :181, that 'the campaign-scoped row is still up' - the test codifies BUG-2 as expected behaviour while its own comment claims 'a caller that guessed at a scope the row does not use is told what it actually cleared'. AC-5's toast clause was checked in the DOM by a MutationObserver and in a test, and never in a painted frame, which is the one place a user reads it. And postureForClass's one-line input guard is simply missing.

NONE OF THIS IS QA BEING WRONG, and none of it is a criterion that needs rewriting. I reproduced all five against the branch build (origin/sdlc/issue-20 at 38982a8) on a fresh database; the evidence[] entries are my own outputs, not QA's. AC-1 through AC-7 are carried forward untouched and are the right contract: the code is wrong, not the criteria, so nothing is renumbered, reworded or dropped, and AC-8 through AC-12 are added for the five defects this PR introduced - which is the only part of this that survives into the next attempt, since QA runs with no memory of what it found last time.

The pattern to record for the Librarian: this repository's failures are not missing checks, they are checks whose fixtures are constructed by the same reasoning as the code they are meant to pin.
work_order.approach:
Move the enforcement, do not add more assertions. Three of the five fixes are the same move - take a property that is currently stated twice and make the second statement impossible - and one of them relocates the gate onto the path that writes.

1. THE WRITE PATH GETS THE GATE AND PROVENANCE (BUG-5). Two mechanisms, both in the executor, both before the provider is reached. (a) PROVENANCE: a delivered envelope must be one this server issued. Look it up by the capabilities primary key (tenant_id, capability_id) - no schema change - and require every signed field plus the signature to equal the stored envelope; a mismatch is refused CAPABILITY_NOT_ISSUED with details.reason 'unknown-capability' or 'altered-envelope'. The signature stops being the authority and becomes what it actually is: proof the bytes have not moved since issuance. (b) THE GATE: rebuild the intent from the STORED envelope and run the SAME pure kernel.validateIntent, with the posture read live from the trust ledger, the approval row named by the envelope's own authority read from the approvals table, and maturity recomputed by the same helper the issuance routes use. The executor takes this as one injected function, and routes.js defines that function ONCE and binds it into the executor and calls it from both issuance routes, so there is one assembly of the gate's inputs in the repository rather than one per call site. This is the plan's rejected alternative taken with the premise removed: it is not a second owner of the check, it is the same function, and what changes is that the values it reads are the server's, not the envelope's.

The envelope grows ONE signed field, `authority`, issued by the kernel from an `approvalId` the caller already holds: {kind:'autonomous'} on /v1/capabilities, {kind:'human-approval', approval_id} on the approve route. It is what tells the executor which approval row to present to the gate, so a pending-but-undecided row can never stand in for a human decision, and it is what the receipt's approval_id is derived from - the caller's claim about its own request is deleted rather than trusted.

2. ONE CANONICAL FREEZE KEY (BUG-3). The kernel exports the derivation of the (scope, scope_id) pair - global and tenant carry the tenant, provider carries the provider id, campaign carries the envelope's resource - and killSwitchChecks is written as a map over that one function. guardian.freeze and guardian.reEnable import the SAME function and default their scope id through it, so a freeze at any of the four scopes writes the key the reader asks for. A caller-supplied scope_id that contradicts the canonical one is REFUSED at the route (400 FREEZE_SCOPE_ID_MISMATCH) rather than written, which closes the hole where it is opened instead of only where it is read.

3. THE RE-ENABLE ANSWERS WHAT IT CLEARED (BUG-2). reEnable returns the row it actually cleared, and a scope that matches no active freeze is a 409 NO_ACTIVE_FREEZE with no row written and no audit event - the same shape the route already uses for a refused re-enable, which the existing test asserts writes nothing. re_enabled becomes true only when a row was active and is now cleared. The existing test at test/api/guardian.test.js:177-181 asserts the opposite and is corrected, not weakened: the case is kept, and what it now asserts is that the lie is impossible.

4. THE DECISION RESULT SURVIVES THE RELOAD (BUG-4). Not 'reload behind a paint' - QA already saw the one frame in five that approach produces, and a toast that flashes for 16ms is not a thing an operator reads. The outcome travels through the reload instead: the success and rejection branches navigate to /approvals with the decision, the receipt id and the reconciliation in the query, and the server-rendered page paints [data-testid=approval-toast] with the identical AC-5 copy into [data-testid=approval-decision-result] and puts the same sentence in #live-region, so the announcement survives the navigation instead of being lost with it. client.js then strips the decision parameters with history.replaceState after the first paint, so a manual refresh does not replay a stale receipt. The duplicate and failure branches are unchanged: neither reloads, and that is why only these two move.

5. ONE INPUT GUARD (BUG-1). postureForClass coerces a non-string action_class to null before the ledger read, so an absent or object value reaches the kernel's existing fail-closed unknown-class branch and answers 403 AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED - the same answer null, a number and an unknown string already get. The refusal already exists; the route is what fails to reach it.

THE RULE THE WHOLE THING RESTS ON: if a value decides whether money moves, exactly one function derives it, and every writer and reader calls that function. Attempt 1 believed a comment plus a hand-computed fixture was an equivalent claim. It is not, and each of the five defects is where that belief was tested by a browser.

files.change: Own the two things the repository currently states twice. (1) A canonical freeze-key derivation - exported, pure, and the ONLY place the (scope, scope_id) pair is computed: global and tenant carry the tenant id, provider carries KILL_SWITCH_SCOPES.PROVIDER_SCOPE_ID, campaign carries the resource. killSwitchChecks becomes a map over it, so the four keys the gate asks for are produced by the same function the guardian writes with, and the two can no longer agree only for the provider scope. (2) A signed `authority` field on the envelope, appended to SIGNED_FIELDS, holding {kind:'autonomous'} or {kind:'human-approval', approval_id}; issueCapability takes an approvalId option and builds it, refuses an approvalId of a kind it does not recognise, and never lets a caller assemble the object. Export one helper that rebuilds a validateIntent intent from a stored envelope, so the executor's re-gate and the issuance routes feed the same pure function the same shape.
files.why: It is already the only place a write is admitted and the only module with no IO; both derivations belong to the deterministic side, and guardian.js importing them is the direction that keeps the kernel pure.

files.change: Two checks between the kill-switch validation and the provider write, both releasing the idempotency claim and returning a stable error on refusal like every other branch. (1) PROVENANCE: repositories.capabilities.get(tenant, capability.capability_id) must return a row whose stored envelope equals the delivered one field by field across the signed fields and the signature; absent is CAPABILITY_NOT_ISSUED reason unknown-capability, differing is the same code with reason altered-envelope. The STORED envelope, not the delivered one, is what the rest of the function acts on. (2) THE GATE: call the injected revalidate function with the intent rebuilt from the stored envelope and the approval id the stored authority names, and refuse on its code - AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED, MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED, CAPABILITY_NOT_ISSUED. Drop the approvalId option and derive the receipt's approval_id from the stored authority instead, so a caller cannot name a different approval on its own receipt. Update the module header's ordered list of checks so the file's own description of the write path is the path.
files.why: The executor is the only module that calls a provider write, so a check that lives only on a minting route is a check no write can reach. The capabilities table already stores every issued envelope, so provenance costs one primary-key read and no migration.

files.change: freeze() and reEnable() stop defaulting scopeId to DEFAULT_FREEZE_SCOPE_ID and derive it through the kernel's canonical function for the scope they were given, so a freeze at global, tenant or campaign writes the key the reader derives. A caller-supplied scopeId is accepted only when it equals the canonical key for a derivable scope; anything else raises FREEZE_SCOPE_ID_MISMATCH rather than writing a row no reader can match. reEnable() returns what it actually cleared - it reads killSwitches.isActive BEFORE the write, refuses with NO_ACTIVE_FREEZE when nothing was active (writing no row and appending no audit event, exactly as a refused re-enable already does), and returns re_enabled:true only when a row went from active to cleared. Keep the actor requirement and the single documented exception (resetSeededKillSwitches) exactly as they are.
files.why: The module's own comment already names the failure this fix removes and then covers only the omitted-scope case; the derivation belongs here because this is the writer.

files.change: Four edits at the composition point. (1) One named autonomyVerdict(tenantId, intent, {nowIso, approvalId}) that assembles kernel.validateIntent's four inputs - live posture, the named approval row, tenantMaturity, nowIso - and is called by POST /v1/capabilities, by the approve route and, through the executor's injected port, at execution; there is no second assembly of those inputs anywhere in the file. risks: The provenance check is the riskiest part of this, and it is deliberate: POST /v1/actions/execute stops accepting any envelope that is not byte-identical to one this server issued, which is a behaviour change for any caller that reconstructs a capability by hand. That is the point (AC-9), but a caller that mints through /v1/capabilities and posts the returned envelope is unaffected, and the two routes the product itself uses are the only callers that matter.

A local database that already holds capabilities issued by the PREVIOUS envelope shape has rows with no `authority` field, so a delivery of one of those is refused as altered-envelope. That is fail-closed and correct, but it will look like a mystery refusal on a machine that has run this branch before. The remedy is to stop the server, delete ./data/app.db together with its -wal and -shm sidecars, and reseed - the same remedy the WAL change already required, and it belongs in the PR body.

Moving the gate onto the write path means the trust ledger is read twice per approval (once at issuance, once at execution) and the approvals table is read once more. All three are indexed primary-key reads on a single-tenant local database, so the cost is immaterial here; a tenant with a large approvals table would want the re-gate to be the same statement the issuance gate already ran, which is recorded in residual_risks rather than assumed away.

Three of the five fixes change what a route answers (409 instead of 200 on a no-op re-enable, 400 on a contradictory scope_id, 403 instead of the 409 default on a gate refusal). Anything downstream that matched the old shape breaks loudly, which is the intent, but the qa_script above is written to the NEW shapes and the previous one is not.

This is the second attempt on a ticket whose first attempt shipped a fourteen-file safety slice, and three of the five defects are in the same three files (kernel.js, guardian.js, executor.js). The change is smaller than attempt 1 but lands in the same high-risk place, so the review stage is where the shape of the fix should be checked rather than after another QA round.

.sdlc/memory/qa/selectors.md and environment.md are NOT updated here - a ticket branch may not write .sdlc/memory/** - and qa_script is a substitute for them, not a replacement. The new decision query parameters, the new FREEZE_SCOPE_ID_MISMATCH and NO_ACTIVE_FREEZE and CAPABILITY_NOT_ISSUED codes, and the fact that a freeze at a non-provider scope now shows a different scope_id in the banner all belong on the Librarian's branch.
out_of_scope: Automatic or deterministic-policy re-enable of a freeze, unchanged from the previous attempt: guardian.recoveryHolds stays exported, named and tested, and nothing in this slice calls it. What changes is only that a re-enable which cleared nothing now says so.

Any live write against the Meta Graph API. live.js still gains no write method, so the blast radius of AC-9 is still an in-memory fake - but the gate is now on the path that would reach one, which is the half that was missing.

Making POLICY_SIGNING_SECRET mandatory outside tests. The dev default stays, because the provenance check means a secret is no longer the authorisation boundary: an offline forger with the correct secret still cannot produce an envelope the capabilities table holds. Changing the boot contract to require the variable would also invalidate the documented QA boot recipe, and that is a decision for a person.

Writing trust_ledger rows in production, account-specific maturity bands, live drift signals, and any second provider. The provider scope id stays a named constant for the reason the previous attempt gave, and the canonical freeze-key derivation takes it as a parameter so a second provider becomes a loop rather than an edit.

Deleting or expunging issued capabilities. The capabilities table stays append-only, so an envelope issued before a reset remains deliverable after it - the same property receipts had before this change, and the reason the reset purges receipts rather than capabilities.

`src/strategy/guardian.js:285`

Evidence: Two-run reproduction against a clean seeded DB (PORT=3112, DB_PATH=/tmp/i20c/app.db), following the work order's qa_script. RUN 1: step 2 mints and executes campaign-status on campaign_001 -> 200. Step 6 raises a global freeze; step 7 re-enables global (200) and raises a campaign_007 freeze. Step 13's `POST /v1/guardian/re-enable {"actor":"owner"}` -> 409 NO_ACTIVE_FREEZE (the provider row was already clear), then the step-0 reset prints 'seed --reset-approvals: purged 0 receipts, released 0 claims, 3 approvals pending, 1 lapsed, 1 kill switch cleared (provider meta_ads)'. RUN 2 on that 'reset' database: `curl -sS /approvals | grep -c guardian-banner` -> 1 (a clean step 0 must show 0); a fresh campaign-status capability on campaign_007 -> 409 KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE after the reset; and `GET /v1/guardian` still lists the campaign row active. The reset is also the printed summary's own contract — the work order's qa_script step 0 requires the line to name 'kill switches cleared', and it names one row while another is still frozen. Test coverage asserts only the provider case: test/data/seed.test.js:116 and :250 both call `repositories.killSwitches.upsertFreeze({scope:'provider', scope_id:'meta_ads', ...})` by hand, so `activeFor(...).length === 0` at :128 and :265 passes without ever exercising a non-provider key — the same fixture-supplies-the-value shape the work order's understanding names as this repository's characteristic failure. Note the pre-fix build behaves the same way at the reset (a global freeze also survives it, under key global/meta_ads), so this is not a new regression; it is a pre-existing gap that BUG-3's fix newly made reachable, because until this PR no route could write a non-provider row that a later run would depend on.

Fix: Derive the cleared rows from the same roster the writer uses rather than from one literal pair — iterate FREEZE_SCOPES and call killSwitches.isActive/reEnable for each canonical key (freezeScopeId already returns the id for global/tenant/provider; the campaign key is not derivable from a tenant alone, so read repositories.killSwitches.listForTenant(tenantId) and clear every active row for the tenant, or clear the three derivable keys plus any active campaign rows). Then report the count of rows actually cleared rather than a constant 1. Add a test that upserts a global and a campaign-scoped row through guardian.freeze and asserts the reset leaves activeFor empty for all four scopes — the existing provider-only fixture cannot fail.

A duplicate delivery arrives UNDER precisely the two conditions admission refuses - a spent nonce and often an active freeze - so identity could not simply be hoisted above the dedupe without breaking AC-2, and the ordering was resolved by leaving the dedupe where it was. src/executor/executor.js:199 reads repositories.actionRecords.getByNonce(capability.tenant, nonce) and returns {executed:false, duplicate:true, receipt_id, reconciliation, drift} before kernel.validateCapability runs at :231 and before the capabilities-table provenance lookup at :244. That lookup's answer describes the STORED envelope's mutation; the body that received it is described by the caller and was never authenticated. Because the lookup is keyed on `nonce` - a value the delivery itself carries - any body at all bearing a spent nonce is answered from the receipt table, and the receipt it is handed is the record of a different mutation. The two gates that would have caught it (the signature, and the comparison against the server's own stored envelope) both live strictly below the branch that returns.

validated_work_order.approach:
Do not add a check. SPLIT THE ONE CHECK INTO ITS TWO ANSWERS, and let the ordering fall out of the split rather than being argued about again. Every version of this plan so far has tried to fix a gap by adding a statement, and every gap has been a statement that was stated in the wrong place.

1. THE KERNEL OWNS TWO NAMED ANSWERS (src/policy/kernel.js). Extract verifyCapabilityIdentity(capability, { secret }) as its own exported pure function holding exactly the MALFORMED_CAPABILITY shape checks and the BAD_SIGNATURE comparison, and have validateCapability call it as its first step before it goes on to expiry, over-scope, replay and the kill switches. One implementation, two call sites - the same shape as version 3's revalidate port, and the same reason: a caller that assembles the check for itself is a caller that can stop calling it. createKernel binds it exactly as it binds validateCapability, so no caller in the repository ever hands a secret to a signing function by hand. The function's own comment states the boundary in one line: identity decides whether the server may TELL you something, admission decides whether you may WRITE, and the two conditions a duplicate arrives under - a spent nonce, a live freeze - belong to admission only.

2. THE EXECUTOR'S ORDER FOLLOWS (src/executor/executor.js). (0) tenant, unchanged. (1) IDENTITY: kernel.verifyCapabilityIdentity on the delivered body. (2) PROVENANCE: the existing capabilities-table lookup and stored-envelope comparison, moved up verbatim, with the STORED envelope acting as it already does from here on. (3) DURABLE DEDUPE: getByNonce, then the atomic claim, both where they are now but three checks lower. (4) ADMISSION: kernel.validateCapability - expiry, replay, kill switches - plus the existing re-gate, both below the dedupe and both before the provider is reached. Two consequences the implementer should not have to rediscover: the release() calls in the identity and provenance branches go away, because no claim is held yet (an unauthenticated body no longer takes the claim, which was a second, quieter exposure on the same branch), and the duplicate branch is now reachable only by a body the server has just proved is its own, so the receipt it returns describes that body by construction rather than by argument.

3. THE DEDUPE ANSWER IS PROVEN BY EQUALITY, NOT BY THE SIGNATURE ALONE. Widen ENVELOPE_FIELDS from ['authority','capability_id','signature'] to every field in kernel.SIGNED_FIELDS, so step (2) requires the delivered envelope to equal the stored one across everything issuance signed. The signature covers those fields today, so this changes no verdict; what it removes is the argument. With only three fields compared, correctness of the duplicate answer rested on the reader of the code knowing which fields the HMAC covers - and the same reader is what put the branch in the wrong place twice. One comparison, whole envelope, no reasoning left to do.

4. NOTHING AFTER THE DEDUPE MOVES. The re-gate and the kill-switch admission stay below it deliberately, and this is the line worth stating once: a delivery that will not write is answered from storage, and a delivery that will write passes every check. That is why a duplicate of a genuine envelope is still answered 200 under a freeze - the operator must not be told their action failed when it succeeded - while any other body is refused before the freeze is even consulted. I applied exactly this shape to the branch and measured it: 425/425 tests pass including the two duplicate cases, and the six repro bodies go 403 while the untampered one stays 200 both with and without a freeze.

5. TWO COMMENTS THAT ARE NOW LOAD-BEARING. The executor's module header already carries an ordered list of the checks and states that the order IS the safety property; renumber it so it describes the path in the file, and fix the kernel.js comment at :19-20 that names a non-existent executor.provenance and claims a property the file did not have. A comment that asserts a safety property is a test nobody runs, and this repository has now been bitten by one twice.

risks: The change makes a previously-answerable request unanswerable, which is the point, and it is the first change in this ticket to make a live endpoint refuse something it used to accept. Any caller that re-delivered a spent nonce with a mutated body was getting a receipt for someone else's mutation; there is no correct behaviour to preserve for it. The two routes the product itself uses are unaffected, and step 14's control clauses exist so QA can tell the two apart.

Extracting verifyCapabilityIdentity is a refactor of a function on the write path, and its whole safety value is that validateCapability's verdict is unchanged for every input it already had. test/policy/kernel.test.js is asked to pin exactly that, input by input, rather than to pin the new function alone - a refactor whose only test is a test of the new name is not pinned.

Widening ENVELOPE_FIELDS from three fields to every signed field changes no verdict today, because the signature already covers them and the identity check runs first. It is included so the duplicate answer's correctness does not rest on a reader of the code knowing which fields the HMAC covers. If it turns out a genuine re-delivery is NOT byte-equal to the stored envelope for some issuance path, the failure will be a 403 on a legitimate redelivery - which is why the untampered duplicate is asserted in three separate suites.

The kernel's re-signing secret is still a published dev default. This change makes that fact harmless for the write path - a correctly signed forgery is now refused on the capabilities table, and step 14(d) drives exactly that request - but it does not make it good, and the boot contract is unchanged. See out_of_scope.

This is the third attempt on this ticket and the second consecutive one to find a defect in the same two files. The previous fix was correct about the design and incomplete about the coverage; the change here is small, but it lands in the same place, so the shape of the reorder is where the review effort belongs.
out_of_scope: Automatic or deterministic-policy re-enable of a freeze, unchanged: guardian.recoveryHolds stays exported, named and tested, and nothing in this slice calls it.

Making POLICY_SIGNING_SECRET mandatory outside tests, unchanged. The provenance comparison now makes the dev default harmless for this surface, which removes the previous attempt's strongest argument FOR changing the boot contract - but changing the QA boot recipe is a person's decision and this ticket does not get to make it.

Any live write against the Meta Graph API, any second provider, and any change to the reconciliation or drift vocabulary. The re-read, the four reconciliation values and the receipt shape are untouched by this change.

Caching, expiry of the stored envelope comparison, or a rate limit on the execute route. The two reads this adds per request are primary-key reads on a single-tenant local database, exactly as version 3 recorded.

Auditing the refused delivery. A body refused at the identity check writes no audit event, as no other refusal on this path does; recording refused attempts is a real question and it belongs to whoever owns the audit vocabulary, not to a bug fix.

The four coverage gaps QA recorded. Second-tenant session isolation, a real provider behind the adapter, the non-approval receipts left in the preview database, and the unreferenced guardian.recoveryHolds are all unchanged by this work order and none of them is what failed.

alternatives_considered.approach: Hoist the whole of kernel.validateCapability above the dedupe, so every check runs before any answer about the nonce
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: I applied it and measured it: it breaks AC-2, and not subtly. validateCapability refuses a spent nonce with REPLAYED_NONCE and an active freeze with KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE, and a duplicate arrives under both by definition, so the honest second delivery would be answered 403 REPLAYED_NONCE. node --test went from 425 pass to 421, with 'a duplicate nonce returns the ORIGINAL receipt and writes nothing' and 'a duplicate is still answered while a kill switch is active' both failing on `false !== true` at the duplicate assertion. This is the approach the previous version's residual_risks argued against in prose; the split is what makes the desired ordering expressible at all.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave the dedupe first and add a full envelope-equality comparison inside the `if (existing)` branch, refusing anything that is not the stored envelope
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It works, and it is the shape this repository has already produced twice: a second copy of the provenance comparison that must be kept in step with the first by hand. It is the 'claim stated twice' diagnosis applied to the fix for the defect that diagnosis produced, and it leaves the unauthenticated body still taking the idempotency claim at :213 before anything has looked at it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Rewrite AC-2 to say that ANY body carrying a spent nonce is answered with that nonce's receipt, making the code correct by definition
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the artefact the pipeline exists to avoid: a criterion rewritten to match a defect, after which every future QA run certifies it. There is no internal contradiction in AC-2 to point at - 'the same capability nonce' is the same envelope delivered twice, and QA's run confirms both halves of that reading independently (the untampered redelivery answers 200, everything else does not). Rewriting it would also delete the only thing that makes a confirmed bug impossible to regress silently.

alternatives_considered.approach: Move the kill-switch check and the re-gate above the dedupe as well, so every gate of every kind precedes every answer
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes AC-2 fail in the case an operator most needs it: a duplicate arriving after the operator has frozen automation would be answered 409, telling them their action failed when it succeeded. The executor's own comment gives the right rule and version 3 preserved it deliberately - a delivery that will not write is answered from storage, a delivery that will write passes every check. 'Every gate before every answer' is a slogan that costs a criterion; the identity/admission split is the property that does not.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make the receipt unguessable (a random receipt id, a per-tenant secret in the receipt) so a delivery that reuses a spent nonce learns nothing useful
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It treats the wrong exposure. The defect is not that a receipt id can be enumerated - it is that the write path tells a caller its mutation is done when the delivery describes a different one, and that a kill switch cannot refuse the delivery because the gate is never reached. Guessing a nonce was never the vector: holding a genuine spent envelope is, and a legitimate caller holding one is exactly who gets a wrong answer.

alternatives_considered.approach: Purge capabilities together with receipts in --reset-approvals, so no spent nonce can outlive a reset
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Carried forward from version 3's rejection and unchanged by this bug: it needs a DELETE on an append-only table to close a hazard nobody has hit, and it breaks the redelivery contract AC-2 is built on. A reset is a QA convenience; the write path must be correct on a database nobody has reset.

assumptions: QA runs against the same seeded single-tenant database shape and the same boot recipe as the previous round. Nothing in this change touches seeding, the trust ledger or the capabilities table's contents, so the fixtures that produced AC-1 through AC-12 still produce them.

The capabilities table remains append-only and is never purged, so a receipt always implies the capability row that produced it still exists. This is what lets provenance run above the dedupe without turning a legitimate redelivery into a refusal; it is stated as an invariant in out_of_scope, and if it is ever relaxed the ordering must be revisited.

A duplicate is answered from the receipt table rather than from the provider, exactly as it is today. The re-read and the provider are still untouched by a duplicate, so nothing about the reconciliation vocabulary changes.
The QA harness still owns the server boot and still runs node scripts/seed.js --reset-approvals against the live database, as the previous attempt assumed and as its own report confirmed.
unknowns: Whether any caller outside this repository re-delivers a capability with a mutated body. Nothing in src/, test/ or scripts/ does, and the route was new in the previous attempt, so this is bounded rather than open - but it is the one behaviour change here that is not merely a bug fix from the caller's point of view.

Whether the issued envelope and the stored envelope are byte-equal in JSON for every issuance path once ENVELOPE_FIELDS is widened. On the two paths in this repository they are - I measured an unaltered redelivery answering duplicate:true with the three-field comparison in place, and the widened comparison is the same code over more fields - but a future path that normalises key order on write would break redelivery rather than a write, which is the safer direction to fail in and the more annoying one to debug.
How a real provider would behave on the re-gate, unchanged from version 3: the only writable provider is the fake, so this defect is verified at the boundary this slice owns.
residual_risks: A duplicate is still answered without consulting the kill switches, and that is deliberate and permanent: the receipt exists, no money moves, and a 409 would tell an operator their action failed when it succeeded. The line is now that this answer is reachable only by a body the server has proved is its own - which is the guarantee version 3 lacked, but the answer is still an answer given while automation is frozen. QA reads this first so that a 200 duplicate:true under a freeze is not filed as a second bug.

The identity check answers 'is this yours' and the provenance check answers 'is this the one you issued' - two mechanisms, and a body that passes both has still not been through validateCapability's expiry check. That is intended (an expired capability's duplicate is still answered, for the same reason a frozen one is) but it means EXPIRED_CAPABILITY is reachable on the write path only for an unspent nonce, which is a fact about the code and not currently written down anywhere.

The executor takes a delivered body and, from the identity check onward, acts on the STORED envelope. If the stored row were ever mutated in place - it is append-only today - the delivered body and the acted-on body would diverge silently. Nothing in this change makes that possible and nothing in it would catch it.

test/executor/executor.test.js's two existing duplicate cases still build their duplicate from the same object the test spent, so they still cannot reach this defect. The new cases build the delivery separately, which is the whole difference; the old ones are kept unchanged as the AC-2 regression net rather than as coverage for BUG-6.

The identity/admission split puts a function in the public surface of the kernel that returns ok for a body it would otherwise refuse. That is a decision, not an oversight, and the kernel test pair that pins both halves is what stops a later reader from 'tidying' it into a single function again.
